hypothesis: The Lahontan datum is a STACK of nested shorelines, not one surface. A tectonic step repeats coherently across two or more levels and lies on one common line; a non-tectonic step (delta topset, fan toe, landslide edge, resistant-bed notch) is local to one level and does not.
mechanism: Bench patches -> tile modes -> a measured block-support level spectrum -> per-level smooth isobase (5.5 km NaN-aware Gaussian, which absorbs post-pluvial isostatic rebound and waterplane tilt) -> residual steps in the 8-140 m throw window -> Hough vote over the flagged pixels of every level, requiring >=2 distinct levels on a common line with sign agreement -> seed a trace, extend it on DEM-ridge evidence, emit dotted lines.
named_non_fault_process_that_could_mimic: Bedrock lithology: a resistant unit that stands as a bench at every lake level crosses several levels at one place and is collinear along strike. Second: isobase-fit error at the margin of a level's extent. Third: a prograding delta / fan that occupied the same position across lake cycles.
